title: WPMS/1905/2013 of Jayesh Ahuja Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No.1905 of 2013
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
Mr. Sanjay Bhatt and Mr. Lalit
Sharma, Advocates for the petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for
the State/respondent no.1.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior
Advocate assisted by Mr. Manoj Sah,
Advocate holding brief of Ms. Geeta
Parihar, Advocate for the respondent nos.2
& 3.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Counter affidavit filed in the Court
today. Same is accepted on record.
Present petition has been filed by the
petitioner for a direction to the respondent
nos.2 and 3 to consider the candidature of
the petitioner for admission against the
vacant seats of Mater of Technology
(M.Tech.) Irrigation and Drainage
Engineering or against other available
seats in other suitable branch in
accordance with law and consequently,
give him admission.
Petitioner applied for Master degree
in Engineering from respondent
University. On 16.07.2013, the respondent
University issued call letter to the
petitioner, directing him to appear in the
counselling. Pursuant to the said call
letter, petitioner appeared before the
counselling board on 15.07.2013, but his
candidature was not considered, as by
that time, result of final semester was not
declared. Second counselling was done by
the University on 06.08.2013 in order to
fill up remaining seats, which could not be

filled up in the first counselling. Petitioner
also appeared before the second
counselling board. He submitted his
application form. In the first counselling,
the petitioner wrote in the checklist that
he secured 52.14% in his B.Tech. degree
programme (appearing). The petitioner
also mentioned in the checklist that the
result of B.Tech. will be declared by the
Pune University by the end of August. His
candidature was not considered in the first
counselling. In the second counselling, the
petitioner wrote in the checklist that he
secured 53.70% in his B.Tech. (Civil
Engineering) degree. Since as per the
Prospectus of the University 2013-14, the
petitioner was not eligible for admission to
M.Tech. degree programme in the
University, as he secured 53.70% marks in
his B.Tech. degree programme, admission
was declined to him. Thereafter, the
petitioner obtained the certificate dated
08.08.2013 issued by the Principal of the
College of Engineering from where the
petitioner did his B.Tech. course. In that
certificate, the Principal has written that
the petitioner has passed his B.E. Civil
Examination, conducted by the University
of Pune in May, 2013 with First Division,
having scored 909/1500 i.e. 60.60%. It
was clarified in the certificate that Pune
University awards degree based on final
year Engineering result and does not
consider the previous year results. The
petitioner submitted that certificate with
the respondent University on 08.08.2013
and prayed for admission. When he was

not granted admission, then he filed
present writ petition.
The contention of the learned counsel
for the petitioner is that since the
petitioner has scored more than 55%
marks in B.Tech. degree, he is entitled for
admission. Learned counsel for the
petitioner submitted that still today, seats
are lying vacant and the respondents can
accommodate the petitioner.
On the other hand, Mr. Rajendra
Dobhal, Senior Advocate for the
respondent nos.2 & 3 submitted that as
per Prospectus of the University 2013-14,
the petitioner was required to deposit his
marks sheet before the Counselling Board.
He argued that since the petitioner in his
second counselling has himself mentioned
in the checklist that he secured 52.14% in
his B.Tech. degree programme (appearing),
which is less than 55%, therefore, no
admission could be given to the petitioner
and there is no illegality on the part of the
University. He also submitted that
counselling as well as admission was
closed on 06.08.2013 and after that, no
admission can be granted to anybody.
I have considered the submission
advanced by the learned counsel for the
parties and have perused the papers
available on record.
Though, I find that petitioner
obtained the certificate dated 08.08.2013
issued by the Principal of the College of
Engineering from where the petitioner did
his B.Tech. course, in which it is
mentioned that the petitioner has passed
his B.E. Civil Examination, conducted by

the University of Pune in May, 2013 with
First Division, having scored 909/1500 i.e.
60.60%, but this certificate was not placed
before the Counselling Board at the time of
counselling. In such circumstances, the
Counselling Board cannot be held
irresponsible. Though, it appears that the
petitioner wrongly calculated his marks
and has wrongly mentioned his marks less
than 55%, but since the counselling is
over and admission is closed, no order can
be passed in favour of the petitioner.
Consequently, the writ petition is
dismissed. However, it will be open for the
respondent University to consider the
application of the petitioner for admission
against the vacant seats on the basis of
his marks, if law permits.
Interim relief application stands
rejected.
No order as to costs.
